source.title: Three Tools for Practical Differential Privacy
source.authors: K. L. Veen; Ruben Seggers; P. Bloem; Giorgio Patrini

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; figures are referenced but their plotted values are not available as text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether differential privacy blocks memorization of random labels while retaining performance on natural labels, using a differential-privacy intervention rather than the original study's comparison.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the reported random-noise training-accuracy comparison and the CIFAR-10 test-accuracy/generalization-gap comparison. Figure-only results for the user-level memorization experiment are not extracted as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares memorization and natural-data learning under private and non-private training, bearing partly on V1. It also directly tests V5 by varying batch size and learning-rate scaling at a fixed 60-epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the memorization experiment but omits the broader conclusion: random-noise sanity checks, adaptive clipping, and large batches with scaled learning rates can make private training and hyperparameter selection more practical. The authors explicitly describe the sanity checks as insufficient for hard privacy guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DPSGD with momentum and a privacy intervention to test memorization and natural-data performance; the original claim compares standard gradient training on natural versus random labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive clipping raises test accuracy from 61.6% to 63.5% at the same privacy budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive gradient clipping can improve differentially private image-classification performance.

record.peer_reviewed: 32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Montréal, Canada
record.problems: The relevant Figure 1 values are not stated numerically in the text; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The random-noise comparison concerns differential privacy, which is not among the claim versions' listed conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 user-level DP-FedAvg pattern memorization results are only shown in the figure; the text gives qualitative outcomes but no accuracy values or explicit measure values that can be extracted as rows. Section 2.1 directs readers to [9] for further details.

untested.parts: Random-label held-out accuracy at chance, quantitatively near-perfect random-label fitting, and the other architectures and ImageNet settings are not established. Random-noise inputs differ from the fixed random-label comparison.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Language models, longer training, warmup, and normalization or regularization remedies are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Four test-accuracy rows: batch 128 with learning rate 0.01, 61.6%; batch 512 with scaled learning rate 0.04, 64.2%; batch 1024 with scaled learning rate 0.08, 66.9%; batch 1024 with base learning rate 0.01, 47.2%. All use small Alexnet on CIFAR-10 with DPSGD for 60 epochs and privacy loss approximately epsilon 20. Privacy noise is calibrated to the budget, so this is a joint batch-size and privacy-recipe comparison.

record.verdict_notes: DP's suppression of memorization is an intervention outside V1's unregularized recipe, so R2 and R5 do not justify an adverse verdict on V1. Figure-only results permit qualitative conclusions where the authors state them, but not invented numerical accuracies.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random-noise memorization and CIFAR-10 natural-label test accuracy for a small Alexnet; does not test the listed small Inception, MLP, or ImageNet settings.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train for 60 epochs on 50,000 random noise examples with non-private SGD and momentum; report training accuracy.
rows.note: The authors state that the non-private model memorizes random noise; no numeric accuracy is given in the supplied text.
rows.check: Qualitative evidence of non-private memorization; the supplied figure text cannot establish nearly perfect training accuracy. Random-noise inputs are used, rather than explicitly reporting natural images with randomized labels.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train for 60 epochs on 50,000 random noise examples with DPSGD extended with momentum; report training accuracy.
rows.baseline: non-private SGD with momentum, figure only
rows.note: The authors explicitly state that DP effectively prevents memorization of random noise; precise plotted values are not supplied.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report that DP prevents random-noise memorization. This changes the training recipe and does not contradict V1's unregularized setting. The rendered delta expression is corrupted and cannot be verified.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 natural labels; report test accuracy and train-test accuracy difference.
rows.note: The authors characterize the real-data performance as capable of learning with a small reduction, but the figure's precise accuracy is unavailable in text.
rows.check: Natural-data learning is supported qualitatively, but exact test accuracy is unavailable in the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 natural labels; report test accuracy and train-test accuracy difference.
rows.measure: Generalization gap (difference between train and test accuracy)
rows.note: The figure reports the gap, but no plotted value is transcribed in the text.
rows.check: A generalization gap alone does not establish V1's memorization-and-generalization comparison. No readable gap value is supplied, and no sharpness measurement links this row to V7.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 natural labels; report test accuracy and train-test accuracy difference.
rows.baseline: non-private SGD with momentum, figure only
rows.note: Authors describe a small reduction in performance relative to the non-private model; precise plotted values are unavailable.
rows.check: The authors report retained natural-data learning. A small reduction relative to non-private performance does not itself make this component of V1 partial. Exact accuracy is unavailable; the rendered delta expression is corrupted.

rows.subject: small Alexnet
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 natural labels; report test accuracy and train-test accuracy difference.
rows.measure: Generalization gap (difference between train and test accuracy)
rows.baseline: non-private SGD with momentum, figure only
rows.note: The figure reports the gap, but the supplied text gives no precise value.
rows.check: A generalization gap alone does not measure any listed version, and its value is unreadable. The extracted partial state has no textual support.

relationships.condition: Non-private small Alexnet trained for 60 epochs on random noise and separately on CIFAR-10.
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 qualitatively support coexistence of memorization capacity and natural-data learning; near-perfect fitting and chance-level random-label test accuracy remain unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Natural-data learning coexisted qualitatively with random-noise fitting, without verified near-perfect fitting or chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
